mstts:express-as.prosody:
Welcome! Have you ever wondered what it’s really like to chase a dream—and still hold on to the parts of yourself that matter most? Life isn’t just about big, show-stopping moments. It’s also about the quiet, behind-the-scenes acts—where ambition, vulnerability, and faith all dance together in ways we don’t always expect.
Imagine the journey of a small-town girl with a voice that could fill a theater, yet a heart that never forgot where she came from. That’s exactly what Kristin Chenoweth shares with us in her book, A Little Bit Wicked: Life, Love, and Faith in Stages. Through her story, we get to see just how unpredictable—and sometimes hilarious—the road to the spotlight can be. There’s dazzling excitement, yes, but also those raw, honest moments when self-doubt creeps in, or when a misstep turns into a story worth telling.
Along the way, we’ll explore how fame, love, and the search for belonging can feel like a balancing act—sometimes risky, sometimes rewarding, but always real. Kristin’s blend of wit, humor, and unwavering belief is the thread that pulls it all together.
As we move through the worlds of Broadway, television, and life’s personal stages, you’ll notice every chapter brings its own lessons and laughter. Faith shows up as both anchor and compass, guiding through the chaos, the applause, and even those silent backstage moments.
So, as we step into this journey together, let’s look for the meaning of success, the beauty of being authentic, and the courage it takes to embrace every single part of who we are. Get ready to discover the magic, the mishaps, and the heart behind every act. Let’s begin.

Chapter One. Growing Up with Big Dreams in a Small Town.
Every journey has to start somewhere, right? For some of us, that beginning is a place where the world feels both welcoming and just a little too small.
Picture a quiet Oklahoma town, where a child with a voice big enough to fill the whole church grew up surrounded by open fields, family, and the slow, familiar rhythm of small-town life. Days drifted by with school, church, and the kind of neighborly kindness where it seemed like everyone was family.
But even with all that comfort, there was always this feeling—like something bigger was out there, just waiting to be discovered.
From the very beginning, music pulled her in. Family get-togethers? They turned into mini-concerts, with relatives urging her to sing just one more song. And the church—well, that became her very first stage. Hymns and gospel tunes weren’t just songs; they were both a source of comfort and her first taste of the spotlight.
There was a sense of belonging, sure, but underneath it all, she knew the world beyond those county lines had so much more to offer.
At home, support was never in short supply. Her parents, practical and grounded in their own ways, saw that little spark in her eyes. So, they made room for it—piano lessons, choir rehearsals, and those gentle reminders that faith and hard work could take her places.
Even the local community got behind her. Teachers, neighbors, friends—they all seemed to know she was meant for something different.
Of course, it wasn’t always easy. In a town where blending in mattered more than standing out, wanting to perform sometimes clashed with the need to fit in. There were days when self-doubt crept in—when the mirror just showed another kid, not a future star.
But through it all, the music never let go. It became her lifeline—a way to express everything that words just couldn’t reach.
As the teenage years rolled around, those dreams only got bigger. Talent shows, school plays, local pageants—they all became stepping stones. Every performance taught her something new—how to handle nerves, how to bounce back from setbacks, and how amazing it feels to truly connect with an audience.
The applause was thrilling, but what really stuck was the sense of purpose that lingered long after the stage lights faded.
Faith was always there, too. In a family where Sunday mornings were sacred, the idea that your gifts are meant to be shared was just part of life. Saying a prayer before going on stage wasn’t about superstition—it was about grounding herself, body and soul.
That belief—that every opportunity was part of a bigger plan—helped her through disappointments and kept her humble during wins.
Looking back, you can see how that small-town childhood was both a foundation and a launchpad. Kindness, perseverance, gratitude—all those values became her anchors as life got bigger and more unpredictable.
And the lessons she learned in those living rooms and church pews? They echoed through every stage she ever stepped on, reminding her that no matter how far you go, your roots always travel with you.

Chapter Two: Finding a Place on Stage and Learning to Stand Out
Leaving behind what’s familiar? That’s never easy—especially when you’re stepping into a world where talent seems to be everywhere, and the competition is fierce.
Imagine being a young performer from Oklahoma, moving from local stages to the big world of musical theater. It’s thrilling, sure, but honestly, it can be a little intimidating too.
For many, college becomes the next big chapter. Suddenly, you’re surrounded by voices that soar, dreams that collide, and a sense that the stakes have never been higher.
Those first days on campus? They’re a whirlwind of excitement mixed with anxiety. You look around, and everyone else was a star back home too. It’s inspiring, but let’s be real—it can also be a bit overwhelming.
The music department practically buzzes with ambition. Every audition feels like more than just a shot at a role—it’s a test of your skill and, sometimes, your self-worth.
There are moments when the pressure gets to you, when you start wondering if you really measure up. But here’s where something important starts to grow: resilience.
Rejection? It used to be rare, but now it shows up more often. And you quickly learn that not every role goes to the most talented person. Sometimes, it’s about timing, connections, or just plain luck.
Learning to accept disappointment without letting it define you becomes a crucial skill. Every setback teaches a bit of humility, and every small win is a reminder—persistence really does matter.
Mentors make a huge difference along the way. Some professors and directors are nurturing, and some are downright tough. But all of them push you to dig deeper—to find something real in every note and every gesture.
The feedback isn’t always easy to hear, but it’s honest. Over time, you realize that true growth means being vulnerable. It’s about being willing to take risks, even if it means failing sometimes.
And then there are the friendships—the ones that start in rehearsal rooms and backstage hallways. These people just get it. They know what it’s like to balance nerves and excitement before a show, to celebrate wins, and to help each other through the tough spots.
Those bonds, formed in the middle of all that ambition and hard work, end up lasting long after the final curtain comes down.
Now, balancing faith in an industry that’s often unpredictable? That’s a challenge, too. Sometimes the values you grew up with seem at odds with the realities of show business. There are moments when you question if you really belong, or if you’ll have to compromise who you are just to fit in.
But holding onto a sense of purpose? That’s what keeps you grounded. Believing your talent is a gift meant to be shared—that’s the steadying force when things get rough.
As graduation approaches, that big question hovers in the air: what’s next? The dream of Broadway calls, but so does the fear of falling short.
Here’s the thing—you start to realize the only way forward is to embrace the uncertainty. To trust that all those lessons—about hard work, resilience, and staying true to yourself—will guide you, no matter where the next stage leads.

Chapter 3. Breaking into Broadway and Navigating Early Success.
You know, the bright lights of New York City can make even the most confident newcomer feel pretty small. Imagine arriving with barely more than a suitcase and a head full of dreams. The city moves fast—sometimes, almost too fast. Suddenly, you’re thrown into grueling auditions, facing fierce competition, and those sky-high living costs? They can keep you up at night.
But under all that anxiety, there’s this electric feeling—like, if you just hang on, work hard, and maybe get a little lucky, anything could happen.
Those first few months? Honestly, they were a total blur. Think open calls that started before sunrise, sharing cramped apartments, and juggling side gigs that paid the rent, but didn’t really feed the soul. Picture waiting in a long line with hundreds of other hopefuls, wondering if this dream is worth all the struggle. There were days when rejection felt personal, when it seemed like the city itself was determined to wear you down.
But every single “no” became a stepping stone—a reminder that grit and perseverance matter just as much as talent.
And then, almost out of nowhere, came a breakthrough. Landing a role in a real Broadway production felt like stepping into another world. The rehearsals were intense—you needed both technical skill and a lot of emotional openness. Surrounded by seasoned pros, the pressure to prove yourself was huge.
Still, something special happened backstage. Cast and crew, all working toward the same goal, started to feel like a family. The laughter, the last-minute rituals, the nerves and excitement of opening night—those moments built a bond that went way beyond personal ambition.
Of course, success brought its own challenges. Suddenly, there was attention from critics, fans, and everyone in the industry. At first, it was thrilling—and honestly, a little overwhelming. Navigating interviews, photo shoots, and all those public appearances meant learning a whole new set of skills. There was this constant tug-of-war between wanting to be your true self and feeling like you had to show a perfectly polished image.
Fame was exciting, but it could also feel surprisingly lonely.
In the middle of all that chaos, staying grounded mattered more than ever. Regular calls home, catching up with old friends, and carving out moments for quiet reflection helped keep everything in perspective. The values learned as a kid—kindness, humility, gratitude—became anchors in an industry that sometimes seemed to reward ego above all else. Faith played a big part, too. Simple prayers before performances, a quiet moment in an empty theater, and the belief that every opportunity was part of something bigger—those things made all the difference.
Not every show was a smash hit, and not every review was glowing. There were disappointments—roles lost, projects that never took off, and times when self-doubt crept in. But each setback? That was a chance to learn, to grow, and to remember why this journey started in the first place.
Because the stage—no matter the risks or rewards—remained a place of real magic. It’s the one space where, for a few precious hours each night, dreams can take flight.

Chapter 4: Balancing Faith, Fame, and Personal Identity
As the spotlight shines brighter, staying true to yourself gets a whole lot trickier, doesn’t it? The entertainment world—where trends change overnight and everyone’s watching—can make you feel like you need to become someone else just to keep up. There are times when the pressure to look a certain way, say all the right things, or just seem more glamorous can feel almost too much to handle. But deep down, that pull to stay authentic never really goes away.
Navigating celebrity life is honestly a series of negotiations. You’ve got publicists, agents, producers—all sharing their thoughts on who you should be and how you should present yourself. Maybe you’ve heard things like, “Try this new look,” or “Let’s highlight this part of your personality.” It quickly becomes this careful balancing act—juggling everyone’s expectations while still honoring what matters most to you.
And then there’s faith. Something that once felt so private suddenly becomes a hot topic in every interview. People are curious, or sometimes even skeptical, and you’re left wondering—should you play it down, or maybe even talk it up to fit the image? But after a while, you realize being open about your beliefs isn’t about convincing anyone or seeking applause. It’s about acknowledging how your spirituality shapes your choices, and how it’s been a source of comfort when things get tough.
Relationships? They get more complicated too. With a jam-packed schedule, it takes real effort to stay close to family and friends. Sometimes it means late-night calls, writing out thoughtful notes, or just finding little ways to be present, even from afar. And let’s not forget romantic relationships—add in the chaos of showbiz and the glare of public attention, and building something lasting feels even harder.
But you know what? There are moments of real joy woven through all of this. That thrill of performing for a live, cheering crowd… teaming up with colleagues you genuinely admire… or using your platform to make a difference—all of that brings a sense of fulfillment that makes the tough moments worth it. Giving back—whether it’s through charity work, mentoring someone new, or simply cheering on others—becomes a way of staying grounded in what means the most.
And over time, one thing becomes crystal clear: authenticity isn’t just a nice-to-have—it’s your real source of strength. Embracing who you are, rather than squeezing yourself into someone else’s idea of “success,” brings confidence and a much deeper satisfaction. Sure, the journey’s messy and far from perfect, but it’s real. And honestly, that’s what makes it all worthwhile.

Chapter 5: Lessons from Setbacks and the Power of Resilience
You know, when we talk about chasing any dream—especially in entertainment—it's easy to imagine a straight shot to success. But the truth is, every journey has its fair share of bumps in the road.
Shows close earlier than expected, roles slip through your fingers, and sometimes, critics just don’t see what you’re trying to do. If you’ve ever gone after something big, you know how tough those setbacks can feel. Honestly, bouncing back from disappointment is just as important as any talent or ambition you might have.
I’ll be real with you—there were moments when rejection stung so badly, it felt almost impossible to move forward. There were auditions that seemed so promising, only to be met with silence. Projects I’d poured my heart into fell apart without any warning. And let’s face it, the temptation to quit and go back to what’s comfortable? It was always lurking.
But every single setback gave me a choice. Would I let disappointment shape my story, or could I use it as a spark to grow?
Let me tell you, resilience wasn’t something I was born with. It’s something I had to build, slowly, one step at a time. What really helped was having the support of friends and family. Sometimes, just hearing a kind word, sharing a laugh, or being reminded that my worth wasn’t tied to any one win or loss—that made all the difference.
Over time, I learned to see every closed door as an invitation to look for something new. And that shift changed everything.
Some of the most powerful lessons actually came from those moments when I felt vulnerable. Admitting I was scared, reaching out for help, being honest about my struggles—it opened up space for real connection and healing. It turns out, everyone—even the people who seem the most successful—faces doubts and challenges. The real difference is in how you respond when things get tough.
Faith played a huge role for me. In those uncertain times, taking a moment for prayer or reflection brought so much comfort and clarity. I started to believe that every experience, whether good or bad, had a purpose. That made it a lot easier to move forward with hope instead of fear.
And you know what else? Practicing gratitude every day shifted my whole perspective. When I focused on what was going right, instead of getting stuck on disappointments, I started to see possibility instead of limitation.
Looking back, it’s the tough moments that really stand out as turning points. Each setback—no matter how painful at the time—led to new insights, and sometimes, to opportunities I never could have imagined.
In the end, the journey wasn’t about being perfect. It was about perseverance—about showing up, doing the work, and trusting that, eventually, the path would reveal itself.

Chapter 6: The Realities of Hollywood—Behind the Curtain.
Picture this—there’s a moment when a dreamer, fresh from the magic of Broadway, steps right into the dazzling lights of Hollywood. It feels a bit like graduating and leaping off a cliff all at once, doesn’t it? Suddenly, you’re surrounded by palm trees, endless sunshine, and a whole new set of rules. The pace picks up, the stakes shoot sky-high, and nothing feels quite as simple as before.
If you’ve ever landed in Los Angeles for the first time, you know the feeling. Auditions, meetings, and those nerve-wracking waiting rooms seem to blur together. Everywhere you look, there are stunning faces and ambition so thick you could almost reach out and touch it. Imagine a young woman—suitcase in hand, script clutched tightly—wandering through a maze of studio lots, wondering if she’ll ever belong. The city buzzes with excitement, but beneath it all, there’s a current of loneliness that’s hard to ignore.
And the work? It’s a whole new ballgame. On stage, every show is alive—here and gone in a heartbeat. But on set, filming is all about stop and start. Scenes are shot out of order, lines change in a flash, and instead of feeding off a live audience, you’re playing to the steady blink of a camera. It’s easy to feel a little lost, to wonder if the spark that once made performing so thrilling can survive this new routine.
But here’s the thing—there are moments that make it all worth it. Maybe it’s a late-night shoot that ends with everyone sharing a meal, laughter ringing out across an empty soundstage. Maybe it’s a director quietly reminding you that even in the middle of chaos, there’s still space for your creativity and heart. Little by little, what felt strange becomes familiar. The city that once overwhelmed you slowly begins to feel like home—a place where your dreams might actually stick.
Still, Hollywood isn’t all sunshine and red carpets. There’s always that push to be thinner, younger, more marketable. Agents and managers share advice, but honestly, sometimes it just sounds like criticism in disguise. It’s so tempting to compare yourself, to wonder if you’re good enough, or worry you’ll be replaced. And in all that noise, it’s easy to forget why you started chasing this dream in the first place.
But here’s something important—if you can hold onto who you are, something changes. There’s a quiet strength that sneaks in. You start to realize that real success isn’t just about landing the next big role. It’s about finding meaning in your work, staying true to your values, and letting the relationships and stories you build outlast all the glitter and glamour. Because in the end, that’s what really lasts.

Let’s talk about something that goes deeper than the applause and the glamour—chapter seven: Love, Loss, and the Search for Belonging.
Even in the brightest spotlight, that longing to truly connect never disappears. Sure, show business brings those electrifying highs, but when you look back, it’s the quieter moments that really stick. Think about sharing a meal with someone who just gets you, those late-night conversations that feel like secrets, or the comfort of holding a hand you trust.
For every roaring standing ovation, there’s usually a night spent alone in a hotel room, asking yourself if all these sacrifices truly make sense.
Now, love in the entertainment world? It’s a whole new level of complicated. Constant travel, unpredictable schedules, and the feeling of always being watched—it’s tough to build something real and lasting. Picture two performers, falling for each other both on and off stage. Their chemistry? Undeniable. But as their careers pull them in different directions, the distance just gets too much.
When the breakup finally happens, it hurts. But here’s the thing—it’s also a turning point. It’s a reminder that love isn’t just about sharing dreams. It needs time, trust, and a willingness to face the hard stuff together.
Family brings its own mix of strength and challenge. Missing birthdays, holidays, and those little everyday moments can leave a heavy ache. Sometimes, the distance feels impossible to bridge. But those early bonds, the ones formed in childhood? They stick. A call from a parent, a letter from a sibling, a quick trip home—these are the moments that remind you what really matters. Fame fades, but family, if you nurture it, endures.
And then there are friendships. In an industry where so many connections feel purely transactional, finding people who genuinely care about the real you is priceless. Maybe it’s that group of friends who meet up for Sunday dinners—telling stories, laughing until it hurts, and just being there when life feels overwhelming. These chosen families remind us that belonging isn’t about where you are, but who stands by your side.
Of course, loss is part of the journey too. Careers shift, relationships end, and sometimes, we have to say goodbye to people we love. Grief can be a quiet shadow or a tidal wave. But even in the midst of sorrow, there’s gratitude—for the love you shared, the memories you carry, and all the lessons along the way.
So, what’s the real takeaway? The search for belonging never really ends. But every connection—no matter how brief—leaves its mark, shaping who we are and reminding us just how much love and loss are intertwined in the human experience.

Chapter 8: Reinvention and the Courage to Change
Have you ever noticed how the path you’re on—one that once felt so right—can suddenly start to shift beneath your feet? Maybe those roles or routines that used to excite you now feel a bit stale. And deep down, there’s this growing urge for something more.
Reinvention isn’t just about making a career move or chasing a new title. It’s really about taking a leap of faith—letting go of what’s comfortable to explore what’s possible.
For some people, that might mean stepping behind the scenes—getting into writing, directing, or producing. For others, it’s about diving into new genres, or picking roles that completely upend old assumptions. Picture an actress who’s always been cast as the ingénue. One day, she decides to go for a role that’s dark, layered, and totally unexpected. The risk? Critics might scratch their heads, fans could be disappointed. But the reward? That spark of purpose comes alive again.
Now, let’s be real—change isn’t easy. There are moments of doubt, and it’s tempting to stick with what you know. The entertainment world especially can be tough—quick to judge, slow to forgive mistakes. But here’s the thing: having the courage to keep evolving, to keep growing, becomes its own kind of success.
It’s not about chasing whatever’s trendy. It’s about tuning in to that quiet voice inside you saying, “There’s more out there waiting for you.”
And faith really does play a part. Believing that every season has a purpose, and that every ending might just be a new beginning, can bring real comfort when things feel uncertain. Prayer, quiet reflection, leaning on the people who love you—those are the things that give you strength to keep moving even when the road ahead is foggy.
When you look back, it’s those moments of reinvention that really stand out—when fear met courage, and the safe, familiar path was traded for the unknown. Those are the turning points, the moments that don’t just define a career, but help shape a calling.

Chapter 9: Giving Back and Finding Meaning Beyond the Stage
As the years go by and the cheers from the crowd start to quiet down, you might find yourself thinking about something deeper—your legacy. What does it really mean to make a difference? How do you take those gifts that brought you success and use them to help someone else?
For a lot of performers, the answer is simple—give back. Maybe it’s mentoring young artists, supporting a cause close to your heart, or speaking up about things that truly matter.
Picture this: there’s a performer who spends her weekends at a neighborhood theater, running workshops for kids who remind her of herself—full of hope, a little nervous, but eager to learn. Watching these kids find their own voices? That kind of joy feels just as powerful as a standing ovation.
Then there are those quiet moments—visiting hospitals, playing benefit concerts, or just offering a small act of kindness that never makes the news, but still manages to change a life.
Giving back isn’t always about the spotlight. Sometimes, it’s honestly the opposite. It takes time, energy, and the courage to step aside and let someone else shine. But here’s the thing—it’s in these moments that real meaning shows up. You start to realize that true success isn’t about the trophies or the applause. It’s about the difference you make in someone else’s life.
And you know what? Faith becomes a guiding light all over again. Believing that every person has a purpose, that every act of kindness matters, really shapes how you live each day. Gratitude turns into a habit—a way to stay grounded, even when everything around you is changing.

Chapter 10: Embracing Wholeness—Life, Love, and Faith in Balance.
After years of chasing dreams, weathering storms, and learning from both triumph and failure, there’s this new feeling that starts to settle in. It’s not about being perfect—it’s about bringing all the pieces of your life together, in a way that feels honest and real.
Imagine waking up one morning. You glance in the mirror, and for the first time, you see not just an actor, or a singer, or whatever role you’ve played, but a whole person. Flawed? Absolutely. Resilient? Definitely. And, most importantly, worthy of love.
Sure, those old anxieties might still whisper now and then, but they don’t get to call the shots anymore. The applause? It’s still sweet, but it’s not the only thing that matters.
Relationships start to go deeper. Friendships that have stood the test of time become real sources of joy and comfort. Even family—where distance and ambition once created tension—those ties get a chance to heal, with understanding and forgiveness growing in their place. Love, in all its forms, turns into a true source of strength, instead of just another distraction.
And faith—well, faith grows up too. It’s not just a list of beliefs anymore. It becomes something you actually live out. It’s how you see the world, how you find hope when things feel uncertain, and how you trust that every single step—even the ones that feel like missteps—are part of something bigger.
When you look back, what stands out isn’t just the roles you played or the awards you picked up along the way. It’s those honest moments, the little acts of kindness, and the decision to keep moving forward, even when things got tough.
In the end, this story isn’t just about one person’s rise to fame. It’s really about all of us—and our search for meaning, connection, and a little bit of grace in our own lives.

As we wrap up this journey—from those first notes in a small-town church, all the way to Broadway’s bright lights and the whirlwind of Hollywood—there’s something that really stands out. A life in the spotlight isn’t just about fame. It’s about daring to dream, holding on through tough times, and finding purpose that goes way deeper than applause.
And honestly, these lessons aren’t just for performers. They’re for anyone navigating big changes, searching for meaning, or just wanting to live more authentically.
So, here’s what you can take with you:
Early support and faith? They’re like anchors when everything else feels uncertain. When rejection or setbacks show up, think of them as invitations to grow, not reasons to give up.
Staying true to yourself—even when it’s tempting to fit in—is a real source of strength. And at the end of the day, it’s your relationships—family, friends, mentors—that define what true success feels like.
Giving back, and living with gratitude? That’s what creates a legacy that lasts long after the applause fades.
The path isn’t always straight. There’ll be times you feel lost, or when the world’s noise drowns out your own voice. But you’re never alone. Every setback is a fresh start, and every act of kindness gets you closer to feeling whole.
So as you move forward, let your story be shaped not just by what you achieve, but by how you love, how you give, and how you stay true to yourself. The stage might change, but the heart of your story—that’s yours to carry.
Keep showing up. Keep singing your song. And trust that the path will reveal itself, one step at a time.
